input.body:
label: bug
file: src/export/scheduler.ts

`nextRunAt` computes the weekly (and monthly) case unconditionally as `from + 7 days` at RUN_HOUR_UTC, unlike the daily branch, which only advances a day when the computed hour has already passed today (`if (next <= from) next.setUTCDate(...)`).

This means that when a weekly schedule is first created, the "next run" is always pushed a full week past the very next occurrence of the run hour, instead of firing on the upcoming Monday at 06:00 UTC if that moment is still in the future. That matches the reports: a schedule created Monday 05:40 UTC (before the 06:00 UTC run hour) should fire that same morning, but instead gets scheduled for the following Monday, silently skipping the first week. The August test case created at 09:00 (after 06:00) happened to work because the "skip a week" behavior coincided with the next real Monday... actually more precisely, the bug reproduces whenever `firstRunAt`/`nextRunAt` is invoked before the daily run hour on the target day for a weekly cadence.

Fix: make the weekly (and monthly) branches only add the cadence interval when `next <= from`, mirroring the daily branch, so the first scheduled run lands on the correct upcoming date instead of one cadence period later.

input.title: Fix weekly scheduled exports skipping their first run
input.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the "weekly" branch always advances by 7 days after setting the hour to `RUN_HOUR_UTC`, unlike the "daily" branch, which only advances a day when the computed run time has already passed (`if (next <= from) next.setUTCDate(...)`). As a result, a weekly schedule created before `RUN_HOUR_UTC` on its chosen day (e.g. 05:40 UTC on a Monday) never fires that same day: the unconditional `+7` pushes its first run a full week out, even though the run time hasn't passed yet. A schedule created after `RUN_HOUR_UTC` correctly waits a week, which is why the August test (created at 09:00) appeared to work while the October one (created at 05:40) did not.

Please add the same "has this run time already passed?" check to the weekly case that the daily case uses, so a weekly schedule created before the run hour on its target day fires that same day instead of a week later, while schedules created after the run hour still wait a full week.
